keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; its New Zealand row begins 1948). The infobox says 'Area: not stated'; the page places the confederation in 'the north of the North Island' and says the Declaration had 52 signatories by 1839, 'mostly from Northland, plus a few from elsewhere, notably Potatau Te Wherowhero, ariki of Waikato Tainui'. Northland (about 10,900 km2 at the grid) is the stand-in; the page names no boundary, and the Waikato signatory did not bring Waikato into the confederation's area.

ledger.note: 1835: northern chiefs declare the independence of New Zealand at Waitangi. the United Tribes declared independence on 28 October 1835 by signing the Declaration of Independence, which Busby had drafted (page, closely paraphrased; British Resident James Busby; the flag had been chosen on 20 March 1834 and gazetted in New South Wales in August 1835). The page says 'the north of the North Island'; Northland is the researcher's reading.

region.text: 'the north of the North Island': the homeland of the northern chiefs who signed the Declaration (most of the 52 signatories were from Northland)

ledger.note: 1840: Britain declares sovereignty over the North Island. Governor William Hobson declared British sovereignty over the North Island on 21 May 1840 (page, closely paraphrased); chiefs met at Waitangi to sign the Treaty of Waitangi in February 1840 (the page gives no day) and the Waitangi Tribunal found in 2014 that the chiefs never agreed to give up sovereignty (page, paraphrased). The confederation is drawn to the sovereignty proclamation.

certainty.note: A confederation of chiefs' lands with no surveyed boundary; Northland is a stand-in.

sources.title: United Tribes of New Zealand
sources.note: Declaration 28 October 1835, flag 1834-1835, signatories, 21 May 1840 sovereignty, Treaty of Waitangi (February 1840).

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks. The page is an 'unrecognized state': Britain recognised the flag in 1836 (the page does not say the state). The Treaty of Waitangi and the competing English and Māori versions are a legal matter the page treats only through the 2014 Waitangi Tribunal finding; this dossier ends the confederation at the 21 May 1840 proclamation (page-dated), not at the treaty. Iwi south of Northland (Waikato, Ngāti Toa, Taranaki and the South Island) are not in the confederation's area; they are covered, from 1858, only for Waikato, by maori-king-movement. The successor slug 'colony-of-new-zealand' needs a dossier (Cliopatria's New Zealand row starts in 1948): counterparts_needing_dossiers. The page's infobox lists the Colony of New South Wales as a successor: New Zealand was administered from Sydney in 1840; not read from a page. No ruler list is given: the page names 'northern chiefs' and Busby only.
